findings: P1 bracketed paste ordering: SshTerminal.ets:374-379 drains every control item before data, while sendPastedText:2076-2081 marks ESC[201~ as control; the paste terminator can overtake queued payload and end bracketed paste early.

P1 IME compatibility: HarmonyOS TextInput onWill/onDid callbacks are documented as system-IME-only, but SshTerminalInputPolicy.inspectSshImeChange always sets sendRemote=false and SshTerminal.onChange never provides a non-callback fallback; third-party IME committed text is dropped.

P1 physical-key fallback: SshTerminal.ets:2527-2536 enables key-code fallback only for a known device id; a keySource=Keyboard event with missing/unrefreshed deviceId and missing unicode falls through to IME/onChange and can be lost or duplicated.

P1 lifecycle generation: SshTerminal.connect publishes state and callback after an await using mutable sessionId (1308-1333), and the callback has no captured session/generation guard; a disappear/re-entry can publish a stale callback or inject queued old output into a new session. The delayed multiline paste callback has the same missing captured generation (2063-2065).

P1/P2 reused-page state: aboutToAppear explicitly allows page reuse (744-750) but does not reset ctrlActive, altActive, shiftActive, kbInput, selectMode or mouse state; sticky modifiers/composition can produce phantom characters and caret state.

P1/P2 TSFN orphan cleanup: StopSshDataRegistration(sessionId,null) (extension_loader_napi.cpp:3663,4032) stops the pump and releases TSFN without clearing the adapter callback retained by registration->adapter; add an explicit adapter stop and stale-registration test. napi_closing in the pump also leaves accepting=true and can churn/drop output after environment close.

P1/P2 output reliability: the bounded native callback queue drops remote bytes at 8 MiB/512 chunks (extension_loader_napi.cpp:6669-6694), while the ArkTS output queue is unbounded (SshTerminal.ets:449-484); no loss/backpressure policy or generation/cap protects terminal fidelity and memory.

P1/P2 reader failure lifecycle: readerLoop stops on libssh2 read error without transitioning connection state (ssh_adapter.cpp:2582-2585); APIs dispatched only while readerRunning can then fail owner routing or direct-call paths after owner death.
